qt: to the Commission Markéta Gregorová (Verts/ALE) Subject:

Foods such as sausages, meat products and sweets are sold on the EU market labelled as ‘for children’ or ‘children’s’, even though they do not fall within the scope of Regulation (EU) No 609/2013 on foods intended for infants and young children. There is no legal definition or specific compositional requirements for products labelled in this way. Their composition often does not differ from ordinary products, including in terms of their salt, fat and additive content – whose intake should be limited in children – and they tend to be more expensive. Consumers, particularly parents, may expect a product labelled as ‘for children’ to be more suitable for children than a standard alternative. Protection against misleading labelling, however, is based on general rules (Directive 2005/29/EC on unfair commercial practices and Article 7 of Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011), the enforcement of which requires proof of the misleading nature of the message in each individual case. 1.
Does the Commission consider the current legal framework to be sufficient to prevent consumers from being misled by such labelling?

Is the Commission considering establishing conditions at EU level for the use of the term ‘children’s’ on ordinary foodstuffs, for example through nutritional criteria, explicit limits on salt, fat and sugar content, or restrictions on food additives?

Does the Commission plan to utilise or update tools such as the nutrient profiles set out in Article 4 of Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006, or to address this issue through legislative initiatives, for example in the area of consumer protection?
